note: EXTENDED Teleon-adjacent competitive due-diligence — a SECOND wave of repos/platforms not in teleon_runtime_landscape.json, classified by capability_slot + a VALIDATION_RISK lens (does this signal STRENGTHEN our thesis, is it SAFE to wrap as a substrate, is it a POSITIONING threat that markets itself near Teleon's surface, or QUARANTINE). Teleon is the capability CONTROL PLANE ABOVE execution substrates: the CapabilityTask/PurposeTask stays STABLE while implementation/runtime evolve, EVIDENCE decides, policy gates promotion, humans approve boundary expansion, predecessors are kept as a lossless rollback target. None of these IS the Teleon runtime. Durable-workflow / compute / edge backends are interchangeable candidates BEHIND ExecutionProviderPort (numeric provider graph + governed fallback): adopting one must NOT create a second durable ledger / second worker framework / second event bus — the Baltor SQLite FleetLedger stays the local truth. Discovery != trust; candidate != active; benchmark/eval result != promotion authority; runtime/agent/LLM output != truth. No raw keys.
positioning_law: Teleon is the capability CONTROL PLANE ABOVE these execution substrates and managed agent runtimes — purpose, capability contract, runtime selection, side-by-side candidates, evidence, eval-GATED promotion, reversible rollback, human boundary approval, truth boundary. Teleon is NOT another agent framework, NOT another workflow/durable-execution engine, NOT another managed agent runtime. We do not compete on 'we run agents'; we win on the capability contract + eval-gated promotion + rollback + truth boundary that sit ABOVE whatever runs the agent.
thesis_signal: The emerging 2026 production pattern is a 2-LAYER stack — Temporal-style macro durable orchestration UNDER LangGraph-style micro agent logic. That split (a stable orchestration/contract layer above a swappable execution layer) is direct external VALIDATION that the control-plane-above-substrate thesis is where the market is converging; Teleon generalizes the top layer from 'orchestration' to 'purpose-defined, eval-gated, runtime-neutral capability'.
execution_provider_port: ExecutionProviderPort — the numeric provider graph (local / function / job / K8s / browser / worker / edge / managed-runtime) chosen by policy/telemetry/pricing with governed, non-silent fallback. Every safe_to_wrap entry below is a candidate node behind this port and carries do_not_adopt_as_primary.

entries.name: Restate
entries.license_note: runtime under BSL (Business Source License, minimal Amazon-style defense); SDKs (TS/Java/Go/Python/Rust) MIT. Single self-contained Rust binary, no external DB, serverless-compatible.
entries.what_it_covers: modern durable-execution engine: workflows-as-code with a command log + event processor, low latency, single self-contained binary, polyglot SDKs; high state + momentum in the Mar-2026 landscape
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: durable-execution primitive only — no capability contract that stays stable while implementation evolves, no side-by-side candidate comparison, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback-as-object, no human boundary approval, no truth boundary
entries.differentiation_move: wrap Restate as a durable-workflow node behind ExecutionProviderPort; Teleon owns the CapabilityTask + evidence + promotion ABOVE the durable log, the log never decides what is promoted
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate durable-workflow backend behind ExecutionProviderPort; the Baltor SQLite FleetLedger stays local truth — adopting Restate must NOT create a second durable ledger / worker framework. Watch the BSL runtime terms before any production reliance.

entries.name: Prefect
entries.license_note: Apache 2.0 (open core; Prefect Cloud is the commercial managed plane).
entries.what_it_covers: mature Python-first orchestration control-plane with a clean separation of orchestration from execution (flows/tasks declared in Python, workers/work-pools run them on chosen infra)
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: orchestrates Python flows, not purpose-defined capabilities; no candidate-vs-baseline comparison, no eval-gated promotion / rollback object, no boundary approval, no truth boundary; orchestration/execution split is structural but not capability-native
entries.differentiation_move: wrap Prefect work-pools as an ExecutionProviderPort node; reuse its clean orchestration/execution split as design CONFIRMATION, but Teleon's stable unit is the CapabilityTask + evidence, not a Python flow
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate orchestration/execution backend behind ExecutionProviderPort; do not let Prefect's scheduler/state become a second control plane or a second durable ledger.

entries.name: Kestra
entries.license_note: Apache 2.0 core (Enterprise Edition is commercial). Declarative YAML-first, event-driven, language-agnostic.
entries.what_it_covers: declarative YAML-first orchestration with a large plugin ecosystem; task runners offload execution to Azure Batch / Google Batch / Cloud Run (orchestration cleanly separated from execution substrate)
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: declarative workflow DAGs, not a self-adaptive capability object; task-runner offload is substrate selection but NOT evidence-gated promotion of candidate implementations, and there is no rollback object / boundary approval / truth boundary
entries.differentiation_move: wrap Kestra (and its task-runner offload targets) as ExecutionProviderPort nodes; its YAML+task-runner split echoes runtime-neutral execution, but Teleon adds the capability contract + eval-gated promotion the DAG layer lacks
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate declarative-workflow backend behind ExecutionProviderPort; its task-runner offload is a backend detail, not a replacement for Teleon's runtime-selection policy or a second durable ledger.

entries.name: Windmill
entries.license_note: AGPLv3 core (backend/), with proprietary 'enterprise' compile-flag snippets; language clients Apache 2.0. AGPL copyleft is a real adoption constraint — wrap behind a process boundary, do NOT link into Teleon's own code.
entries.what_it_covers: script-platform + growing workflow engine: turns scripts into webhooks/workflows/UIs, fast self-hostable execution engine
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: script/workflow execution platform, not a purpose-defined capability plane; no candidate comparison, eval-gated promotion, rollback object, boundary approval, or truth boundary
entries.differentiation_move: wrap Windmill as a script-execution node behind ExecutionProviderPort via a service boundary (never an in-process import, because AGPL); Teleon's CapabilityTask + evidence stay the stable layer
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate script/workflow backend behind ExecutionProviderPort ONLY across a service boundary (AGPL); not a second control plane or durable ledger.

entries.name: Flyte
entries.license_note: Apache 2.0, LF AI & Data Foundation-governed (not single-vendor-owned).
entries.what_it_covers: Kubernetes-native ML pipeline orchestration; strongly typed tasks/workflows, reproducibility, and built-in data lineage for ML pipelines and data assets
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: ML/data pipeline orchestration with lineage, but lineage != evidence-gated promotion; no stable capability contract above evolving implementations, no candidate-vs-baseline, no rollback object / boundary approval / truth boundary
entries.differentiation_move: wrap Flyte as a K8s-native ML-pipeline node behind ExecutionProviderPort; adopt its type-safety + data-lineage as CONFIRMATION that lineage matters, but Teleon's receipts + eval-gated promotion sit above Flyte's lineage
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate ML-pipeline backend behind ExecutionProviderPort; its lineage is a substrate facet feeding Teleon evidence, not the promotion authority or a second control plane.

entries.name: Ray / Ray Serve
entries.license_note: Apache 2.0. Ray Serve = scalable, framework-agnostic model-serving + Python business logic on a distributed runtime.
entries.what_it_covers: scalable distributed compute + model-serving backend; framework-agnostic online inference and arbitrary Python serving at scale
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: raw scalable compute/serving — no capability contract, runtime-selection policy, candidate comparison, eval-gated promotion, rollback object, boundary approval, or truth boundary
entries.differentiation_move: wrap Ray Serve as a compute_backend node behind ExecutionProviderPort; Teleon decides WHICH candidate implementation Ray serves and whether it is promoted, Ray just executes
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate scalable-compute/serving backend behind ExecutionProviderPort; a serving cluster is not a control plane and must not become a second worker framework or ledger.

entries.name: Modal
entries.license_note: proprietary serverless cloud (Modal Labs); open-source CLIENT libraries only — the platform is hosted/closed. Network + account required.
entries.what_it_covers: serverless GPU/CPU compute for AI/ML workloads; fast container scale-up, scale-to-zero, code-first serverless functions on a hosted cloud
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: managed serverless compute, not a capability control plane; no contract/selection/evidence/promotion/rollback/boundary/truth layer, and it is proprietary cloud (no local-equivalent fallback by itself)
entries.differentiation_move: wrap Modal as ONE serverless compute node behind ExecutionProviderPort (peer of local/function/K8s); Teleon keeps a local-equivalent fallback so a Modal outage degrades gracefully and never owns truth
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate serverless-compute backend behind ExecutionProviderPort; proprietary cloud — never the primary runtime, always one switchable peer with a governed local fallback, never a second control plane.

entries.name: Cloudflare Workflows (+ Durable Objects)
entries.license_note: managed edge platform (proprietary cloud); the 'Dynamic Workflows' library is MIT. Durable Objects = per-object SQLite-backed durable state at the edge.
entries.what_it_covers: durable execution engine for multi-step apps at the edge: task queueing + scheduling on Durable Objects, per-tenant/per-agent dynamic workflow code, hibernation/resume
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: edge durable-execution substrate, not a capability plane; no capability contract, candidate comparison, eval-gated promotion, rollback object, boundary approval, or truth boundary (note: Cloudflare AGENTS is a separate, positioning-threat surface — see below)
entries.differentiation_move: wrap Cloudflare Workflows as an edge_durable_runtime node behind ExecutionProviderPort for low-latency/edge tasks; Teleon's contract + evidence + promotion stay central and runtime-neutral
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate edge-durable-execution backend behind ExecutionProviderPort; proprietary edge platform — one switchable peer, never the control plane or a second durable ledger.

entries.name: LangGraph (OSS micro agent orchestration)
entries.license_note: OSS LangGraph library is MIT (LangGraph 1.2, May 2026: agent run = durable graph execution via checkpointer/StateSnapshot + persistence + HITL + streaming). The MANAGED LangGraph Platform is a separate commercial offering — see positioning threats.
entries.what_it_covers: micro-orchestration of agent logic as a durable, checkpointed state graph: persisted transitions, replay-from-checkpoint, pause-for-human, streaming
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: micro agent-logic layer only — no purpose-defined capability contract spanning runtimes, no candidate-vs-baseline selection, no eval-gated promotion, no rollback-as-object, no boundary approval, no truth boundary; it is the BOTTOM layer of the 2-layer stack, not the control plane
entries.differentiation_move: treat the Temporal(macro)+LangGraph(micro) 2-layer pattern as external PROOF of control-plane-above-substrate; Teleon generalizes the top layer to a runtime-neutral, eval-gated CAPABILITY contract and can host LangGraph graphs as one candidate implementation

entries.name: Letta (MemGPT lineage)
entries.license_note: Apache 2.0 (formerly MemGPT, UC Berkeley). Python agent runtime with tiered core/recall/archival memory, agent-as-OS model, served as an API.
entries.what_it_covers: agent memory runtime: persistent tiered memory (core/recall/archival) so agents remember/learn/self-improve over time; runs LLM agents as long-lived services
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: memory/state for a single agent, not a capability control plane; no capability contract, runtime selection, candidate comparison, eval-gated promotion, rollback object, boundary approval; memory recall != governed truth (Baltor-style truth boundary still required)
entries.differentiation_move: wrap Letta as an agent_memory_runtime candidate behind a memory port (peer of mem0/supermemory); Teleon/Baltor govern whether recalled memory is truth and which agent implementation is promoted — Letta serves memory, it does not decide promotion or truth
entries.do_not_adopt_as_primary: candidate agent-memory backend behind a memory provider port; its recalled memory is candidate context, never auto-served truth, and it is not a second control plane.

entries.name: LangGraph Platform (managed)
entries.license_note: commercial managed runtime (tiers on the LangChain pricing page) for long-running stateful agent workflows with autoscaling + SLA; the underlying LangGraph library is MIT.
entries.what_it_covers: managed deployment + autoscaling + persistence/recovery + SLA for long-running, stateful 'durable agents' — marketed close to 'an agent runtime'
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: it RUNS durable agents; it does not declare a stable capability contract across runtimes, generate side-by-side candidate implementations, gate promotion on EVIDENCE, keep a predecessor as a reversible rollback target, require human boundary-expansion approval, or enforce a truth boundary — and it is tied to the LangGraph programming model
entries.differentiation_move: do NOT compete on 'we run agents': Teleon sits ABOVE LangGraph Platform — the capability contract + eval-gated promotion + rollback + truth boundary that hold whether the agent runs on LangGraph Platform, Temporal, or a Cloud Function; LangGraph Platform is one candidate runtime, Teleon decides if its output is promoted

entries.name: Cloudflare Agents SDK
entries.license_note: Agents SDK (github.com/cloudflare/agents) on the Cloudflare edge; each Agent IS a Durable Object with its own SQLite DB. Project Think (Apr 2026) adds durable-execution primitives (fibers/stash/recovery).
entries.what_it_covers: persistent, stateful agent execution environments on Durable Objects: per-agent state/storage/lifecycle, scheduling, WebSockets, MCP, workflow integration — explicitly 'build stateful AI agents / durable agents'
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: it hosts durable agents at the edge; it does not declare a runtime-neutral capability contract, compare candidate implementations against a baseline, gate promotion on evidence, keep a reversible rollback target, require human boundary approval, or enforce a truth boundary; it is bound to the Cloudflare runtime
entries.differentiation_move: Teleon is the control plane ABOVE Cloudflare Agents — wrap it as one edge agent runtime candidate, but the stable CapabilityTask + evidence + eval-gated promotion + rollback + truth boundary live in Teleon, not in the Durable Object

entries.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
entries.license_note: proprietary AWS managed runtime; GA Oct 13 2025. 8-hour execution windows, session isolation, A2A protocol, and (Mar 2026) durable managed session storage that resumes filesystem state by session id.
entries.what_it_covers: managed runtime to deploy/operate agents at scale on any framework/model/protocol: long execution windows, session isolation, durable session storage, enterprise VPC/PrivateLink
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: it securely runs/operates agents; it does not own a stable, runtime-neutral capability contract, side-by-side candidate comparison, evidence-gated promotion, reversible rollback object, human boundary approval, or a truth boundary — and it is AWS-proprietary/cloud-locked
entries.differentiation_move: Teleon stays the cloud-neutral control plane ABOVE AgentCore: AgentCore (or Vertex Agent Engine) is one managed-runtime candidate behind ExecutionProviderPort; Teleon's capability contract + eval-gated promotion + rollback + truth boundary remain portable across both clouds

entries.name: Google Vertex Agent Engine (Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform)
entries.license_note: proprietary Google Cloud managed runtime; at Cloud Next 2026 Vertex AI Agent Builder was rebranded into the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — Agent Engine = the managed runtime (compute-billed per vCPU-hour, persistent memory, enterprise governance).
entries.what_it_covers: managed agent runtime + ADK + Agent Studio + 200+ models + persistent memory + tool governance, billed on compute consumption — marketed as the enterprise agent runtime
entries.what_it_lacks_vs_teleon: it runs/operates agents and even adds 'tool governance', but it does not own a runtime-neutral capability contract, side-by-side candidate comparison vs a baseline, evidence-GATED promotion, reversible rollback object, or a Baltor-style truth boundary — and it is GCP-proprietary/cloud-locked
entries.differentiation_move: Teleon is the cloud-neutral control plane ABOVE Vertex Agent Engine: wrap it as one managed-runtime candidate, differentiate on capability-contract + eval-gated promotion + rollback + truth boundary that stay portable across GCP/AWS, NOT on 'we run agents'
